title.name: Base ARES
title.tagline: Junior astronaut training at Base ARES

howTo.title: How to play
howTo.move: Move with WASD or the arrow keys. On a phone, drag the joystick.
howTo.use: Walk to a glowing station and press USE (E or Space).
howTo.follow: Follow the yellow arrow to your next stop.
howTo.bubble: Bubble will tell you what each room does!

hud.doseDetail: Crew radiation dose: 0–100 game units, not real dose. Mars lacks a thick atmosphere and global magnetic field to block particles.
hud.polygonsDetail: Triangles rendered per frame, including rendering passes

data.title: Mission data
data.barsNote: Integrity and Oxygen starting values and damage are provisional game rules. The Energy bar shows how much of today's need your plan covers.

bubble.name: Bubble
bubble.welcome: Hi, I'm Bubble! Welcome to Base ARES on Mars. Follow the yellow arrow!

room.control: The Control Room is the heart of the base. We plan every Sol from here.
room.weather: The Weather Station watches wind, temperature and pressure on Mars.
room.lab: In the Laboratory we study rocks and dust. Science time!
room.greenhouse: Plants grow here. Look, they get bigger every Sol!
room.lifeSupport: Life Support keeps our air fresh so we can breathe.
room.comms: Communications sends messages all the way to Earth. Hi, Earth!
room.shelter: The Magnetic Shield refuge has thick walls. We hide here during solar storms.
room.observatory: From the Observatory we watch the Sun and the sky.
room.airlock: The Airlock is the door to the outside. Suits on before going out!
room.shield: The Magnetic Shield protects the base. Its reinforced refuge keeps the crew safe.
room.solar: The solar panels supply our game energy budget.

bubble.tourDone: You visited every room. Great job, junior astronaut!
bubble.night: It's getting dark. Look up, can you spot Earth? It's the tiny blue dot!
bubble.report: New Sol! Let's read today's space report together.
bubble.plan: Now go to the Energy Panel in the Control Room and share all the available energy.
bubble.start: Systems on! Follow the yellow arrow to your tasks.

alarm.sep: Alert! Energetic particles! Run to the Magnetic Shield refuge!
alarm.cme: Alert! A CME may hit Mars! Let's go to the Shelter.
alarm.flare: Alert! A strong solar flare! Let's be safe in the Shelter.

bubble.noImpact: The Sun is active, but this storm should not reach Mars. Phew!
bubble.safe: We're safe in the Shelter. Great running!
bubble.taskTry: Good try! We learn every time.
bubble.sumGood: Great planning! The base is happy.
bubble.sumBad: Oops, some systems needed more energy. Let's plan better next Sol.
bubble.energyFirst: Plan the energy first at the Control Room.

report.title: Sol {{n}} Report
report.dateNote: Sol {{n}} uses data captured on Earth date {{date}}. This pairing is a story choice: an Earth day and a Mars Sol are not the same length.
report.weatherWhere: Measured by the InSight probe in Elysium Planitia, not at Base ARES.
report.fallback: No temperature reading: a standard game value is used.
report.sunActive: The Sun is active, but this storm should not reach Mars.

info.show: Where does this number come from?

energy.title: Energy Panel
energy.hint: Use all the energy. Free energy must be 0 to start.
energy.budgetNote: The 100 kWh base budget is a game rule, not a real measurement.
energy.dustNote: Simulated panel dust reduces this Sol's pool by {{loss}}%. Clean the arrays to restore future output.

T02.name: Classify the Flare
T02.goal: Tap the flares from weakest to strongest.
T02.fact: Each letter is 10 times stronger than the one before. X flares can go beyond X10!

T03.name: CME Arrival
T03.goal: Drag to today's CME speed to see when it would reach Mars.
T03.dist: Mars is about 1.524 AU from the Sun: about 228,000,000 km.

T04.name: Check the Forecast
T04.enlilNo: WSA+Enlil forecast: no impact on Mars.
T04.noSim: There is no WSA+Enlil forecast in today's data.

T05.name: Go to the Shelter
T05.goal: Reach the Magnetic Shield refuge before time runs out!

T06.name: Mission Control Reading
T06.goal: Which message talks about today's main event?

T07.name: Thermostat
T07.goal: Outside it is {{t}} °C. Set the heater so we stay cozy at {{tin}} °C inside.

T08.name: Wind Rose
T08.goal: Tap the direction the wind came from most often.

T10.name: Photo Album
T10.goal: Pick the right caption for this picture.
T10.sampleArt: Drawn placeholder: a real NASA photo will go here.

T15.name: Recycle Water and Air
T15.goal: Send each item to the right machine.

photo.rover: A rover driving on red Martian rocks
photo.dustDevil: A dust devil spinning across Mars
photo.olympus: Olympus Mons, the biggest volcano on Mars

alarm.title: Space weather alert!
alarm.goShelter: Go to the Magnetic Shield refuge!
alarm.adjust: You can also adjust energy at the Control Room.

summary.title: Sol {{n}} summary
summary.sparks: The shield was weak: sparks hit the domes!

consequences.allClear: Recovery complete. Base systems are returning to normal.

kinds.solarBody: A solar particle event is separate from Martian weather. Follow the shelter guidance.
kinds.lifeSupportBody: Cold and low oxygen need attention.
kinds.dustBody: Simulated dust can cover the solar arrays.
kinds.greenhouseBody: The plants need energy and care.
kinds.perfectBody: Every system received the right energy.

storm.title: Simulated Martian dust storm
storm.cause: Trigger: {{wind}}. This is a game simulation, not a NASA dust measurement or a solar flare.
storm.effect: Dust is covering the arrays. Inspect and clean the most-soiled group first to protect the next Sol's energy.

shield-deficit.title: Magnetic Shield deficit
shield-deficit.cause: You gave the shield {{allocated}} kWh; it needed {{demand}} kWh, leaving {{missing}} kWh missing. Solar reading: {{flare}}.
shield-deficit.effect: Electronics flicker and crew dose rises by {{dose}} game units. Shelter timeout penalty: {{penalty}}. Integrity effect: {{integrity}}.

life-deficit.title: Cold Life Support
life-deficit.cause: Life Support received {{allocated}} of {{demand}} kWh. InSight AT mean: {{temp}} °C; colder air increases the existing heat demand.
life-deficit.causeNoTemp: Life Support received {{allocated}} of {{demand}} kWh. No AT reading was available, so the labeled game fallback set demand.
life-deficit.effect: Cold cabins and frost slow oxygen generation. Oxygen effect: {{oxygen}}.

greenhouse-deficit.title: Greenhouse underpowered
greenhouse-deficit.cause: The Greenhouse received {{allocated}} of {{demand}} kWh, leaving {{missing}} kWh missing.
greenhouse-deficit.effect: Leaves droop, grow lights dim and oxygen contribution falls. Oxygen effect: {{oxygen}}.

solar-dust.title: Solar arrays dusty
solar-dust.cause: Simulated storm wind: {{wind}}. Average array dust is now {{dust}}%.
solar-dust.effect: Next Sol's energy pool loses {{loss}}%, capped at 20%. This is a game rule, not measured dust opacity.

solar-cleaned.title: Solar output restored
solar-cleaned.cause: Every array was inspected and cleaned in priority order. Remaining average dust: {{dust}}%.
solar-cleaned.effect: The panels shine again. Next Sol's dust loss is {{loss}}%.

energy-surplus.title: Extra energy vented
energy-surplus.cause: A system received more energy than it needed. Surplus never adds dose or reserves.
energy-surplus.effect: The gentle venting glow is harmless, but that energy could help another system.

perfect-sol.title: Perfect Sol!
perfect-sol.cause: Every system is in its ideal energy band and the crew completed the plan.
perfect-sol.effect: Warm lights, ripe apples and {{integrity}} Integrity / {{oxygen}} Oxygen regeneration, using the existing task reward.

gameover.title: Mission paused
gameover.body: The base needs help. Let's train again!
gameover.evacuated: The crew evacuated safely. No one was hurt on screen; use the cause below to train again.

radiation.title: Radiation limit reached
radiation.body: The crew dose reached 100 game units. The shield needed more energy or the crew missed shelter.

suffocation.title: Oxygen depleted
suffocation.body: Oxygen reached zero. Life Support and the Greenhouse did not receive enough energy.

powerCollapse.title: Base integrity lost
powerCollapse.body: Integrity reached zero after the Magnetic Shield deficit. The crew evacuated before further danger.

cert.title: Junior Astronaut Certificate
cert.body: {{name}} kept Base ARES safe for 5 Sols!
cert.local: Your nickname stays only on this device.

start.attention: Sol {{sol}}: the Sun is busy today!

narrator.cme: A CME is traveling at {{v}} km/s.
narrator.cmeNoImpact: A CME left the Sun at {{v}} km/s, but it should not reach Mars.
narrator.alert: Let's hurry to the Magnetic Shield refuge!
narrator.dustStorm: A simulated dust storm is using the {{v}} trigger; clean the arrays before sealing.

consequences.shield-deficit: The shield received {{a}} kWh but needed {{d}}, so dose rose {{dose}} game units.
consequences.life-deficit: Life Support received {{a}} of {{d}} kWh, leaving the cabin cold.
consequences.greenhouse-deficit: The Greenhouse received {{a}} of {{d}} kWh, so growth and oxygen slowed.
consequences.solar-dust: Simulated dust reduces the next energy pool by {{loss}}%.
consequences.solar-cleaned: The cleaned arrays restored future solar output.

narrator.hint: Hint: today the {{system}} needs the most energy. Look at the report!

summary.good: Great planning, every system was happy!
summary.reveal: The ideal plan was Shield {{s}}, Life Support {{l}} and Greenhouse {{g}} kWh.

answers.what_is_a_flare: A solar flare is a super bright flash on the Sun. Scientists sort them by letters: each letter is 10 times stronger than the one before!
answers.why_shelter: Some space storms send fast tiny particles. The shelter has thick walls that keep astronauts safe until it is over.
answers.why_cold_energy: The colder it is outside, the faster our base loses heat. So the heaters need more energy to keep us cozy!

ask.title: Ask Bubble
ask.why_shelter: Why do I need a shelter?
ask.why_cold_energy: Why does cold use more energy?

observatory.title: Observatory
observatory.unavailable: No authentic image is available for this sample date.
observatory.archiveNote: A real picture from NASA’s archive. It is not tied to this Sol’s sample date.
observatory.explanation: A window into the Universe, recorded by scientists and photographers.

refine.imageFailed: This picture could not load. Let’s try another window into space!
refine.nasaMore: APOD shares astronomy pictures. The NASA library collects images from space missions. Picture dates belong to Earth, not to our game’s Sol clock.

walk.control: Find the coral Energy Panel by the wall.
walk.observatory: The violet door leads to the sky watchers.
walk.shield: The blue door leads to our protective shield.
walk.lifeSupport: The teal door leads to fresh air and warmth.
walk.greenhouse: The green door leads to our growing plants.
walk.solar: Go through Life Support and the Airlock to the yellow solar park.

garden.learning: Plants grow food for the crew. They also help keep the air fresh.
garden.cosmetic: Just for fun — apples do not change mission energy or rewards.

mini.retryBody: Nothing was lost. Your station is ready for another try.
mini.practice: Snapshot practice — not a reading from this Sol.
mini.practiceLearned: This practice used a labeled snapshot rather than an observation from this Sol.
mini.rulesNote: Puzzle targets, timing and stars are provisional game rules.
mini.constantSpeed: Simplification: constant speed over the mean Sun–Mars distance, not an actual arrival forecast.
mini.weatherInspired: GAME RULE inspired by Mars weather
mini.returnControl: Return to Control to seal the report.
mini.sealGoal: Match the levers to your confirmed energy plan.
mini.taskNarration: You completed {{task}} with {{mistakes}} mistakes in {{seconds}} seconds.

SortFlares.name: Sort the Flares
SortFlares.goal: Tap the class cards from weakest to strongest: A, B, C, M, X.
SortFlares.readingHint: The letter is the class; the number is its strength within that class.
SortFlares.instruction: Tap one card at a time. It goes straight into the next space.
SortFlares.orderLabel: Flare classes from weakest to strongest

PhotoDetective.name: Photo Detective
PhotoDetective.goal: Match the source caption to the picture.
PhotoDetective.decoyMap: A floor plan of Base ARES

AlignCoils.name: Align the Coils
AlignCoils.goal: Turn each pointer toward its triangle mark.
AlignCoils.learned: In this game, the coil pointers match the marked targets.

WireShield.name: Wire the Shield
WireShield.goal: Join endpoints with the same color and symbol.
WireShield.learned: In this game, matching symbols identify connected wires.

CmeCountdown.name: CME Countdown
CmeCountdown.goal: Match the recorded speed, then choose the travel time.
CmeCountdown.learned: The snapshot records a CME speed of {{value}} km/s.
CmeCountdown.arrival: Choose the rounded constant-speed travel time (hours).

PipeFlow.name: Pipe Flow
PipeFlow.goal: Tap each pipe until it turns green, then send the flow.
PipeFlow.learned: The game routes reach their marked oxygen and water tanks.
PipeFlow.instruction: Tap a pipe to rotate it. Cover the dashed guide; green means connected.
PipeFlow.ready: All pipes connected. Send the flow!
PipeFlow.keepGoing: Rotate every pipe that is not green yet.

ThermostatDial.name: Thermostat Dial
ThermostatDial.goal: Read the temperature and match the game heating requirement.
ThermostatDial.learned: The InSight snapshot records an average of {{value}} °C.

SmartFarmCare.name: Smart Farm Care
SmartFarmCare.goal: Water the beds, adjust the light, then pick ripe apples.
SmartFarmCare.learned: This game care sequence uses water, light and ripe-apple targets.

CleanPanels.name: Solar Array Rescue
CleanPanels.goal: Inspect each array, clean the most-soiled one first, then verify restored output.
CleanPanels.learned: Dust lowers the next Sol's game energy by at most 20%; complete cleaning restores output.
CleanPanels.instruction: Start with the highlighted, most-soiled array. Tap its brush once for each required pass.
CleanPanels.restore: Full maintenance restores the next Sol's output.
CleanPanels.alreadyClean: Every array is clear. Verify the restored photovoltaic shine.

TiltSun.name: Tilt to the Sun
TiltSun.goal: Turn the panel onto the highlighted game angle.
TiltSun.learned: The highlighted angle comes from the game’s simulated Sun.

IrrigationPlan.name: Share the Water
IrrigationPlan.goal: Subtract each bed moisture from the target and share the drops.
IrrigationPlan.learned: Distributing only the missing water avoids waste.

ResourcePriority.name: Life Support Priorities
ResourcePriority.goal: Below full oxygen, restore air; otherwise compare heating and greenhouse demand.
ResourcePriority.learned: Life support prioritizes the resource that needs attention.

PowerBalance.name: Power Check
PowerBalance.goal: Compare the available bar with the combined system demands.
PowerBalance.learned: Comparing supply and demand helps us plan without changing the budget.

WindReading.name: Read the Wind
WindReading.goal: Choose the compass direction written in the snapshot.
WindReading.learned: Reading weather supports maintenance; this is not a sensor at Base ARES.

dataNotes.flare: Class recorded in the DONKI snapshot. A missing reading uses a training snapshot.
dataNotes.temperature: Average air temperature recorded by InSight, not a sensor at Base ARES.
dataNotes.wind: Wind direction from the InSight snapshot. Without a reading, the task uses a training snapshot.

challenge.rewardNote: Continue confirms the existing game reward.
challenge.impactQuestion: Can this picture alone tell us whether a storm reaches Mars?
challenge.impactAnswer: No. We need the DONKI forecast for Mars.
challenge.observeQuestion: Which description belongs to this picture?
challenge.forecastYes: The snapshot forecasts an impact at Mars.
challenge.forecastNo: The snapshot does not forecast an impact at Mars.
challenge.matches: The available budget covers the demand
challenge.shortfall: The demand exceeds the available budget

SortFlares.happening: The shield needs the recorded flare class.
SortFlares.importance: Class letters help us interpret the solar alert.
SortFlares.hint: Follow the cards above the spaces: A first, then B, C, M and X.
SortFlares.error: That card is not next. Follow A, B, C, M, X from left to right.

PhotoDetective.happening: The telescope shows a NASA archive picture.
PhotoDetective.importance: A source caption describes what was observed, not a storm warning.
PhotoDetective.hint: Match the source title, then consider what a picture can prove.
PhotoDetective.error: That caption is not the source title, or a picture alone cannot predict an impact.

AlignCoils.happening: The snapshot sets the shield alert level.
AlignCoils.importance: Aligned game coils prepare the protective station.
AlignCoils.hint: Each triangle is the target for its pointer.
AlignCoils.error: A pointer still misses its triangle target.

WireShield.happening: The shield circuit needs matching connections.
WireShield.importance: Correct connections prepare the shield during the Sol alert.
WireShield.hint: Follow both the symbol and the color.
WireShield.error: These endpoints have different symbols and colors.

CmeCountdown.happening: The snapshot records a CME speed.
CmeCountdown.importance: Travel time is a simplified estimate, not an impact forecast.
CmeCountdown.hint: Match the recorded speed and its constant-speed time.
CmeCountdown.error: The speed or time does not match the recorded speed calculation.

PipeFlow.happening: Air and water circuits need their correct routes.
PipeFlow.importance: The station keeps the crew supplied with air and recycled water.
PipeFlow.hint: Tap each pipe until the colored line covers the dashed guide and the card turns green.
PipeFlow.error: Some pipes are not green yet. Rotate those pieces before sending the flow.

ThermostatDial.happening: The InSight snapshot supplies the outside temperature.
ThermostatDial.importance: Heating demand changes with the temperature in our game.
ThermostatDial.hint: Use the displayed heating requirement, not the temperature as kWh.
ThermostatDial.error: Your lever does not match the heating requirement calculated by the game.

SmartFarmCare.happening: Some training beds need water before harvest.
SmartFarmCare.importance: Careful irrigation avoids watering beds that are already moist.
SmartFarmCare.hint: Read moisture, water only thirsty beds, then set light and harvest.
SmartFarmCare.error: This bed already has enough training moisture.

CleanPanels.happening: A labeled simulated storm can leave four solar arrays dusty.
CleanPanels.importance: Cleaning the most-soiled arrays first protects the next Sol's energy pool.
CleanPanels.hint: Use the highlighted brush. Light dust needs one pass, heavy dust two, and buried arrays three.
CleanPanels.error: Finish the highlighted array before moving to the next one.

TiltSun.happening: The game Sun marks a panel orientation.
TiltSun.importance: This calibration prepares the solar park without inventing generation readings.
TiltSun.hint: Align the panel with its highlighted angle.
TiltSun.error: The panel angle does not match the highlighted game target.

IrrigationPlan.happening: The training tank has a limited water supply.
IrrigationPlan.importance: Distributing only the missing water avoids waste.
IrrigationPlan.hint: Subtract each bed moisture from the target and share the drops.
IrrigationPlan.error: A bed has too much or too little water; check its moisture.

ResourcePriority.happening: Read current oxygen and the Sol heating demand.
ResourcePriority.importance: Life support prioritizes the resource that needs attention.
ResourcePriority.hint: Below full oxygen, restore air; otherwise compare heating and greenhouse demand.
ResourcePriority.error: Check oxygen first, then compare the displayed energy demands.

PowerBalance.happening: The park provides the existing game energy budget.
PowerBalance.importance: Comparing supply and demand helps us plan without changing the budget.
PowerBalance.hint: Compare the available bar with the combined system demands.
PowerBalance.error: Compare the total demand with the available budget, not a single system.

WindReading.happening: The InSight snapshot records a prevailing wind direction.
WindReading.importance: Reading weather supports maintenance; this is not a sensor at Base ARES.
WindReading.hint: Choose the compass direction written in the snapshot.
WindReading.error: That direction does not match the recorded prevailing wind.
